data.name: Ayd
data.gender_notes: Ayd is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Arabic root 'Awd', meaning to help or support. In Islamic history, Ayd was the name of a companion of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh) known for his generosity and kindness. The name Ayd carries the meaning “Helpful” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Ayd usually hope their child will grow to embody helpful and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Carry the light of kindness and support for others.
data.etymology: Ayd belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Helpful.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Ayd total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_arabic.name: أيد
in_arabic.long_meaning: أيد هو اسم عربي يعود إلى جذور قوية في اللغة العربية، ومشتق من الفعل أيد الذي يعني النصر والغلبة والقوة، ويحمل هذا الاسم معنىً روحياً كبيراً في الإسلام، حيث يرتبط بالعون الإلهي والقوة الروحية

in_urdu.name: ایڈ
in_urdu.long_meaning: ایڈ کا نام عربوں کے لیے ایک مقدس نام ہے جو عربی زبان کے gốc سے لیا گیا ہے، اور اس کا مطلب مدد و حمایت اور قوت ہے، اور یہ نام برصغیر پاک و ہند میں بھی بہت مقبول ہے

in_hindi.name: अयद
in_hindi.long_meaning: अयद नाम का अर्थ सहायता और शक्ति का प्रतीक है, और यह नाम भारतीय मुसलमानों में बहुत लोकप्रिय है, और इसका महत्व इस्लामी परंपरा में बहुत अधिक है

in_pashto.name: ایډ
in_pashto.long_meaning: ایډ د افغانستان او پښتنو لپاره یو مقدس نوم دی چې د عربي ژبې څخه اخیستل شوی، او دا نوم د مرستې او ملاتړ په معنا دی، او دا نوم په افغانستان کې ډیر مشهور دی

data.cultural_impact: The name Ayd is rich in cultural significance, embodying the Islamic values of kindness, generosity, and support within a community. Ayd was the name of a remarkable companion of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh), often known as Ayd ibn Hatim, who displayed exceptional acts of generosity and support towards his people. This companion's story serves as an inspiration and reminder for the importance of compassions and kindness towards others, encapsulating the spirit of Ummah (global Muslim community).
data.spiritual_significance: In a spiritual context, the name Ayd conveys the meaning of being a Helper or Supporter to the divine plan. It is a reminder of the importance of being of service to others, to the community, and, ultimately, to Allah, as per one of the Islamic names of Allah, Al-Hafeez (The Protector). The name Ayd can be seen as a call to be a beacon of support and kindness in one's personal and communal life, fostering a deep bond with the Creator and creation.

historical_references.reference: Ayd al-Khurrasani: A Persian poet and scholar who lived during the Abbasid Caliphate era (750-1258 AD). He is best known for his works on Quranic exegesis, poetry, and Sufism.
historical_references.context: A prominent scholar and poet during the Islamic Golden Age.

historical_references.reference: Eid al-Adha: A major Islamic holiday celebrated annually to commemorate the willingness of the Prophet Ibrahim to sacrifice his son, Isma'il, as an act of submission to God. The name 'Eid' translates to 'festival' in Arabic, and is celebrated during the Hajj pilgrimage.
